reference.scope: S2-54: shared texture load palette/key/raw subresource copy helpers. Device7 destination mip chain may be any complete subset of source levels, with source-relative rectangle/point coordinates divided for every source level (floor origins, ceil ends); validate all source cube faces before copying selected flags, zero cube flags copies nothing, ordinary 2D ignores face flags, source/destination coordinate objects unchanged. Mip descriptors mark MIPMAPSUBLEVEL and GetAttachedSurface accepts caps2-only mip queries. Device7 copies existing palette tables only when both palettes exist and copies every present color key while preserving absent destination keys. Legacy Texture1/2 copies common mip prefix, requires a destination palette when source has one, retains palette identity, copies source-blit key only and preserves destination keys when absent on source; clears ALLOCONLOAD for visited levels including missing-palette failure prefix. Shared raw copy bypasses surface clipper/key filtering, preserves exact mip/face addressing, synchronizes external memory and returns transport errors with accepted prefix retained. Portable actual C9671 checks,384 frozen Windows/Wine cases,20 runtime mutations, old actual frontends plus new helpers runtime control, ASAN/UBSAN including signed-overflow bounds. XP complete constructors/COM interfaces:60 surface nodes over9 textures (two cubes),35 uploads,29 fills,23 raw/probe copies,29 actual readbacks and5 refusals. Covers two selected versus four retained cube faces at3 mip levels, 2D mip subset offset2, Texture1/2 differing mip lengths with suffix preservation, palette table/identity, metadata and input immutability. Replies acknowledge transport only; separate real GPU replay verifies1037 pixels across29 images, exact9 explicit resource destructions and empty guest resource/device maps before owner release. CPU surface rows retain existing8-byte alignment including1x1 readback padding; wire uploads are tightly packed. Legacy cube support is the existing project extension, not a native Texture2 cube oracle. Bounded negative/NULL/sublevel guards and returned transport errors do not reproduce native crash or silent-error quirks. Partial cube construction, palette/key inheritance/restrictions for arbitrary public sublevel calls, full formats/compression/callback/thread/loss/Reset/wrapper conversion, S2-55/57, native HAL, games/FPS and review stages4/5/6 remain open. The shared host cube allocator now grants renderable, uncompressed ordinary cube textures the same blit/clear attachment usage as 2D textures, without changing public usage flags; BC formats remain non-attachments. Protocol ABI, shader semantics and D3D8/9 DLLs are unchanged. Graphics bundle rebuilt and synchronized to9335ee9a77fb7cc808d2; CPU core assets remain byte-identical.

previousHost.expectedFailure: ordinary cube storage lacks RenderAttachment; the actual GPU command encoder rejects the colour-fill pass

validationRepairs: The first CRT-free SDK exceeded the Windows small-frame stack threshold; palette arrays now use static storage so the executable retains no CRT stack-probe dependency.

The initial helpers returned explicit named HRESULT failures without the existing diagnostic trace wrapper. The retained diagnostic suite caught this; all such returns were annotated, native/mutation/sanitizer/domain/strict builds repeated and the final XP capture is fresh. The earlier capture/source is retained under stage4i9-first-diagnostic-control.

The initial wire reader assumed a tightly packed1x1 readback. Existing DirectDraw CPU rows are8-byte aligned. The reader and GPU row indexing now assert the actual CPU pitch/byte count, while uploads remain tightly packed.

Actual GPU replay exposed a shared host defect: ordinary non-render-target cube storage lacked the attachment usage needed by colour fills, invalidating the command encoder and all eighteen cube images. The cube allocator now follows the existing2D renderable/noncompressed eligibility. New fake-device colour-attachment validation covers RGB/indexed cubes at every face/mip and compressed exclusions; the same captured trace also reproduces the old-module failure with eleven non-cube images still correct.

The new executor case now flushes its buffered frame before inspecting actual attachment views, and treats omitted base mip/layer fields as their API default zero. This harness correction changes no production behavior.

Protocol and shader semantics are unchanged; rebuilt graphics files and worker revision prefixes are all synchronized. CPU assets are verified against both the core build and the previous site commit.
